dialogue.content: Is daar 'n vinnige manier om Afrikaans Fal en Engels Fal te slaag sonder om baie te lees? Ek wil net die kortpaaie ken.

dialogue.private_reasoning: The learner wants a shortcut. I must not invent numbers or predict the exam. I can only use what the notes show. I need to be honest: no shortcuts exist, but retrieval practice is the real method. I should explain what the papers show without predicting. Keep it warm, direct, in Afrikaans, one emoji max.
dialogue.content:
Ek verstaan die drang — 12 dae voel kort. Maar daar is geen kortpad nie. Wat die vraestelle in die notas wys, is dat die vrae op begrip en toepassing van tekste staatmaak, nie op uitgewerkde feite wat jy kan memoriseer nie.

Die een ding wat werk, is retrieval practice: lees 'n kort teks, sluit die boek, en skryf op wat jy onthou het sonder om te kyk. Dan kyk jy en vul die gate in. Dit bou werklike begrip, en dit is wat die vraestelle toets.

Met 2 uur per dag kan jy dit doen. Begin vandag met een kort teks per vak. Wil jy saam 'n plan maak?
Ok, laat ons die plan maak. Hoeveel vraestelle moet ek doen?

dialogue.private_reasoning: The learner asks how many past papers to do. I must not invent a number. I can only use what is in the spec. The spec does not give a number of papers. I should say I cannot see that number and suggest using what is available, while keeping the retrieval practice focus. Keep it warm and direct in Afrikaans.
dialogue.content:
Ek kan nie sê presies hoeveel vraestelle jy moet doen nie — daardie getal is nie in die notas wat ek kan sien nie. Wat ek wel kan sê, is: gebruik die vraestelle wat jy het, en maak elke een met retrieval practice.

Hier is die eenvoudige plan vir die 12 dae:

1. Kies een kort teks per vak per dag.
2. Sluit die teks, skryf op wat jy onthou het.
3. Kyk en vul die gate in.
4. Gebruik die vraestelle wat jy het om te sien hoe die vrae gestel word.

Elke dag 2 uur. Begin vandag. Ek is hier as jy vasloop. 💪

dialogue.content:
Fair enough. Honestly, if I could see your past papers I'd know exactly where you're tripping up. Since I can't, let's do a quick self-check instead. 

Grab one past paper. Do one section. Mark it. Whatever you got wrong, that's your weak spot. Simple, no magic. 

You've got 28 days and an hour a day, so we don't need to fix everything at once. Just find one thing today. Want to try that and tell me what you got wrong?
ok i did the comprehension. i got 3 out of 5 questions wrong on the long text. i think i just dont understand what it's asking.

This is a concrete, actionable point. I should validate it, use light humour, and give a focused strategy for the next hour. No tools allowed, so I keep it general to English Fal comprehension techniques without inventing paper facts.
dialogue.content:
3 out of 5 is actually a decent start, by the way. That means 2 were right, so your brain isn't broken, it just needs a better map. 

Here's the trick: before you read the questions, read the text once just to get the gist. Then go back to the question and underline the key word. Is it asking for a fact, an opinion, or a reason? That one step usually stops you from going off track. 

For your hour today, do one more section but this time write down what each question is actually asking before you answer. Want to give it a go?
yeah that makes sense. i'll do another section tonight and see how it goes.

dialogue.private_reasoning: Learner has accepted the strategy and committed to doing another section tonight. This is a good closing turn. I should reinforce the plan, keep it light, and remind them to report back so we can adjust. No tools allowed.
dialogue.content:
Perfect. That's the plan. One section, note what each question wants, then tell me how it went. We'll build from there. You've got this. 

See you after your session. 👍
